text:
acme-support: Hey team — over the past hour our p99 latency jumped from ~120ms to ~600ms. We're pinned to eu-west-1 but our distributed traces show ~30% of requests taking a route that lands in us-west-2 before returning. Happening across multiple clients. Anyone seen weird cross-region hops recently?

jessica: Thanks — sorry about the hit. Can you paste a couple of trace IDs and a sample request (headers) so we can check routing and fallback logic? Also which SDK / agent version? :thinking_face:

acme-support: Trace IDs: trace-0a1b2c3d and trace-0f9e8d7c. Using our internal client v1.12.0 (calls via Redwood hosted API). Sample header we add: `X-Client-Region: eu-west-1`. No custom routing headers otherwise.

jessica: Got it. Sending to telemetry to pull the traces. In the meantime can you repro with `curl -v` and include `X-Request-ID`? Quick check: are you using `region: nearest` or explicitly `region: eu-west-1` in the request config?

acme-support: We're explicitly setting region=eu-west-1 in our SDK config (not nearest). Repro steps: 1) send 1000 small generation requests over 2 mins 2) sample the high latency ones 3) capture response headers. Will attach a small `curl` we used: 

```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west-1" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: acme-test-123" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rw-large","input":"hi"}' -v
```

leo-oncall: Telemetry pulled the spans. There's a consistent intermediate hop showing `egress-proxy-usw2` appearing in the trace when the path crosses regions. Adding sample span snippet: `span:egress|host:egress-proxy-usw2|latency:240ms`. Looks like smart-routing picked a fallback route to a cheapest compatible egress pool, but that shouldn't happen for pinned region. Investigating routing policy evaluation. :rotating_light:

samir-netinfra: Can you also share the customer's account id? Need to check per-tenant routing overrides and any recent changes to egress pools or peering. Also checking peering flaps between eu-west-1 and our global backbone.

acme-support: account acme-9987. Also noticed that when the SDK retries we see a different host header in the second attempt: `x-forwarded-region: eu-west-1` on successful ones, but the slow traces show `x-forwarded-region: us-west-2` on the egress span.

jessica: Okay that suggests routing decision changed post-auth or during retry. Two hypotheses: 1) auth tokens validated in eu but the request got routed to a cheaper cross-region egress due to a transient capacity shortfall in eu cluster; 2) a mis-evaluated fallback policy treating eu variant as unhealthy and selecting a global fallback that routes via us-west-2.

leo-oncall: I'm running a targeted repro from our infra: forcing 500 concurrent requests with header `X-Client-Region: eu-west-1` and `X-Request-ID: leo-repro-01`. Collecting full traceroute from the serving node to the egress. If you can run same from your side and post the traceroute output that's ideal.

acme-support: Pasting one high-latency traceroute (from their client):

```
traceroute to api.redwood.ai (13.224.11.45), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1 (10.0.0.1)  1.123 ms  0.950 ms  0.912 ms
 2  52.16.12.1 (52.16.12.1)  12.456 ms 12.332 ms 12.540 ms
 3  * * *
 4  52.95.34.22 (52.95.34.22)  120.234 ms 121.111 ms 119.987 ms
 5  15.197.44.10 (15.197.44.10)  240.890 ms 241.002 ms 240.745 ms
 6  egress-proxy-usw2.redwood.internal (3.5.2.11)  242.100 ms 242.250 ms 242.050 ms
 7  13.224.11.45 (13.224.11.45)  244.300 ms 243.900 ms
```

samir-netinfra: That traceroute is very telling — a hop into our `egress-proxy-usw2` pool mid-path. Looking at recent deploys: we rolled a new autoscaler config for eu egress pools 1.5 hours ago that temporarily marks capacity as `soft-full` earlier to shift load. It's possible the smart router is selecting a cross-region egress to avoid tail latencies. I see an incident ticket on the autoscaler tweak: INC-4891. Rolling back the soft-full heuristic would prevent cross-region diversion.

jessica: For immediate mitigation, we can add a per-tenant override to prefer intra-region egress for acme-9987 until the autoscaler fix. I'll push a temporary policy: `egress_policy: prefer-local` for that account. Samir, can you coordinate the rollback?

samir-netinfra: Will do. Rolling back autoscaler flag now and applying the per-tenant override. ETA ~6 minutes.

telemetry-bot: [automated] applied policy override: `egress_policy=prefer-local` for tenant acme-9987 at 2026-03-17T15:08:34Z. Observability: sampling rate for traces increased.

leo-oncall: Early indicators — acme's p99 dropped from ~600ms to ~140ms for new requests after override. Still monitoring for residual in-flight retries.

acme-support: Seeing improvement on our side, thanks. We'll keep an eye and report if it resurfaces. Can you also share the postmortem or roll details for the autoscaler change once available?

jessica: Yes — Samir will add notes to INC-4891 and we'll share a short blameless postmortem with timeline + mitigation steps. For follow-up: (1) make autoscaler change less aggressive for pinned-region tenants, (2) add unit tests / sim to catch region-diversion behavior, (3) surface an alert when >5% of traces for a tenant show cross-region egress.

samir-netinfra: Adding postmortem and follow-ups to the incident. Thanks for the quick repro and traceroute, that made root cause straightforward.

acme-support: Appreciate the fast help — saved our important rollout. :heart:

jessica: Great teamwork. Re-opening channel if anything else pops up. (reaction: :white_check_mark:)
